claims.text: Aluminum and vanadium are lightweight, high-strength alloying elements.
Alloying titanium with aluminum and vanadium can produce a solid material with superior comprehensive performance and reduced weight.
The proposed intervention is alloying titanium with 6 wt% aluminum and 4 wt% vanadium.
The alloy is to be fabricated by powder metallurgy followed by hot isostatic pressing at 900°C and 100 MPa for 2 hours.
The proposed alloying and processing route will refine the grain structure.
The proposed alloying and processing route will produce a uniform distribution of aluminum and vanadium.
The refined grain structure will strengthen the alloy through grain-boundary strengthening.
The addition of aluminum and vanadium will strengthen titanium through solid-solution strengthening.
The proposed material will have a 25% higher yield strength than pure titanium.
The proposed material will have a 15% lower density than pure titanium.
A 10% increase in yield strength and a 5% reduction in density define the stated performance boundary.
Performance may vary with processing conditions and alloy composition.
Secondary phases may precipitate during heat treatment.

contradictions.description: The baseline is labeled "Pure titanium (Ti-6Al-4V)." Ti-6Al-4V is also the modified composition specified by the intervention, so it cannot simultaneously denote pure titanium and the alloy being compared against pure titanium.
